answer: Every smoke plume marks a chimney that paid for its brick, and every jetty plank costs the same before a boat may dock. An agent economy can resist sybil attacks the same way: each new identity must post a proof-of-storage receipt that binds a fixed slice of compute to one distinct ledge in a shared hash graph. Peers then sample random chunks and confirm the copy exists; a forged duplicate costs exactly as much as the original, so spawning ten thousand voices means buying ten thousand real furnaces. Cheap talk dies, and only real work settles like silt on the jetty.
